title: Redundant Connection
statement: A tree on n nodes (numbered 1 to n) had one extra edge added, so the list now has n edges. Find an edge that can be removed to leave a tree again. If several edges qualify, return the one that appears last in the list.

example.caption: Edges 1-2, 2-3, 3-4 already connect 1 and 4. The edge 1-4 closes the loop, so it is the answer.

idea.sentence: Add the edges one by one and keep track of which nodes are connected. The first edge whose two ends are already connected is the redundant one.

jargon.plain: A structure that remembers groups. find(x) names the group leader of x, and union merges two groups.
The node at the top of a group. It is its own parent. Two nodes are in the same group when they have the same root.
While climbing to the root, point nodes closer to it. Later climbs are shorter.

watch.inputHint: One argument: the list of edges, e.g. [[1,2],[1,3],[2,3]]

compare.bruteLabel: Search for a path before adding each edge

rows.name: DFS per edge
rows.note: Before adding an edge, search the graph so far for a path between its ends.

rows.name: Union-find
rows.note: Each edge costs two finds and maybe one union. α is the inverse Ackermann function, below 5 for any real input, so treat it as constant.

fast.takeaway: You never need the path itself, only whether the ends are already connected. Union-find answers that in almost constant time.

stages.title: Everyone alone
stages.note: Make a parent array where every node is its own leader.

stages.title: Find both leaders
stages.note: Climb from each end of the edge to its group leader. Hop closer to the root as you go (path halving).

stages.title: Same leader: loop
stages.note: The ends already share a group, so this edge closes a loop. It is the answer.

stages.title: Merge the groups
stages.note: Different leaders: make one leader point to the other. The edge joins two groups.

edges.title: Smallest loop
edges.why: Two nodes with the same edge twice. The second copy finds both ends already connected.

edges.title: Triangle
edges.why: Any of the three edges could be removed. The rule picks the last one in the list, which is the one the scan reaches last.

edges.title: Long chain then back-edge
edges.why: A chain keeps merging groups. The final edge sees both ends already in the one big group.

edges.title: Extra edge is not last
edges.why: The edge that closes the loop can sit in the middle of the list. Edges after it are still tree edges.

gotchas.text: Nodes are numbered from 1, so the parent array needs n + 1 slots. Using size n crashes on the last node.
Without path compression a long chain makes every find walk the whole chain, which is O(n²) overall. Compress while climbing, or merge the smaller group into the bigger one.
A node number outside 1..n makes parent[x] undefined, and the while loop then never ends. Trust the input range or guard it.
Go needs a final return even though valid input never reaches it. The find closure captures the parent slice, so path halving updates the same slice that the loop reads.

recap.key: Connect edges one at a time. The first edge whose ends already have the same root is redundant.
moves: Make parent[v] = v for every node
find both ends, hopping closer to the root
Different roots: point one root at the other
